e.etymology: The Scandinavian and Hungarian spelling of Camilla, the feminine of the Roman family name Camillus; a camillus was a noble youth who assisted at religious rites. Virgil's Camilla is a warrior maiden in the Aeneid.
The feminine form of Hebrew adir, meaning mighty, noble or majestic.
A Biblical Hebrew name, Chaziel, God sees or vision of God, borne by a Levite in 1 Chronicles. In the US it is used mostly in Spanish-speaking families.
From an English surname that began as a medieval pet form of Eustace. As a girl's name it is treated as a short form of Anastasia, Greek for resurrection, and it peaked in the 1970s.
namesakes: Stacy London (What Not to Wear co-host)

assoc.t: Stacy's Mom, 2003 hit by Fountains of Wayne
Stacy's pita chips
internet slang for a stereotyped popular, attractive woman

e.note: Stacy's Mom jokes are common, and online Stacy is slang for a stereotyped popular girl.

e.etymology: From Arabic ayman, on the right hand and so blessed or fortunate; it shares a root with yumn, good fortune.
A medieval variant of Aylmer, from Old English Aethelmaer: aethel (noble) plus maere (famous). It survived as a surname and returned as a first name in the 19th-century United States.

assoc.t: Elmer Fudd, Bugs Bunny's hunter foe
Elmer's glue

e.note: Closely tied to Elmer's glue and Elmer Fudd, and widely heard as an old-fashioned name.

e.etymology: From the English word noble, from Latin nobilis, well known or high-born. It was a familiar first name in 19th-century America, taken from both the word and the surname.
The Italian word giada, jade, used as a given name in modern times; it is the Italian counterpart of the English name Jade.

assoc.t: Giada De Laurentiis, TV chef known by her first name

e.etymology: The Biblical Kenan was a great-grandson of Adam; his Hebrew name is often read as possession. In Turkey and Bosnia the same spelling is the name Canaan, and in English it can be a form of Keenan.
namesakes: Kenan Thompson (Saturday Night Live cast member)

assoc.t: Kenan & Kel, 1990s Nickelodeon sitcom

e.etymology: A modern American name built on Kyle with an -in ending, in the family of Kylan and Kyler. Kylin is also an English spelling of qilin, a hooved creature of Chinese myth.
A respelling of Rory, the English form of Irish Ruaidhri, from ruadh (red) and ri (king). In the US the -i spelling is given almost entirely to girls.

assoc.t: Rory Gilmore of Gilmore Girls (spelled Rory)

e.etymology: A German blend of Maria and Lene, short for Magdalene. Marlene Dietrich, baptized Maria Magdalene, made it famous, and the wartime song Lili Marlene spread it further.

assoc.t: Marlene Dietrich, classic film star

e.etymology: A Spanish and Italian pet form of Carmen and Carmel, names honoring Our Lady of Mount Carmel. The mountain's Hebrew name, Karmel, means garden or orchard.
namesakes: Carmela Soprano (Tony's wife on The Sopranos)

assoc.t: Carmela Soprano, Tony's wife on The Sopranos

e.etymology: A spelling of Arabic Hakim, wise or judicious, from the root for wisdom and judgment. Al-Hakim, the All-Wise, is one of the names of God in Islam.
namesakes: Hakeem Olajuwon (Hall of Fame NBA center)

assoc.t: Hakeem Olajuwon, Hall of Fame NBA center

e.etymology: A Biblical Hebrew name, Amaryah, Yahweh has said or promised, borne by several priests and Levites. In the US it goes mostly to girls, where it also reads as Amari with the -iah of Mariah.
A pet form of Kenneth, the English form of two Gaelic names: Coinneach, handsome, and Cinaed, often read as born of fire.
namesakes: Kenny Rogers (country singer of The Gambler)

assoc.t: Kenny McCormick, the hooded kid on South Park

e.etymology: From an English surname and place name: Old English Cena, a man's name, plus leah, a woodland clearing. It also arose as a shortening of McKenley, a variant of McKinley.
A spelling of Amara with a final h. Amara has several separate sources, among them Igbo amara, grace, and Sanskrit amara, immortal.
A modern American coinage that joins Ice to the popular -lynn ending, on the pattern of Jocelyn and Roselyn.
A respelling of Malachi, from Hebrew Malakhi, my messenger or my angel. Malachi is the last of the twelve minor prophets of the Old Testament.
A name used mainly in Mexican American families, built with the -beth ending of Elizabeth and Lizbeth. The first part is of uncertain origin.
A Latinate form of Evangeline, the name Longfellow made famous in his 1847 poem. Both come from Latin evangelium and Greek euangelion, good news or gospel.
A modern American blend of Riley and Lynn, one of many names built on the -lynn ending.
A form of the Biblical Uzziel, Hebrew for God is my strength, as it is written in Greek and Latin Bibles. It is used mostly in Mexican and Brazilian families.
From Arabic hasan, good or handsome. Hasan ibn Ali, grandson of the Prophet Muhammad, made it one of the most widely used names in the Muslim world.
namesakes: Hasan Minhaj (comedian and Patriot Act host)

e.etymology: A short form of Anselm, from the Germanic elements ans (a god) and helm (helmet, protection). It also came down as the English surname Ansel or Ansell.
namesakes: Ansel Adams (landscape photographer of the American West)

assoc.t: Ansel Adams, landscape photographer

e.etymology: A variant of Isidora, the feminine of Greek Isidoros: the goddess Isis plus doron, gift. The name outlived the worship of Isis and was borne by early Christian saints.

assoc.t: Isadora Duncan, pioneer of modern dance

e.etymology: The feminine of Hebrew Ziv, radiance or brightness. A separate Slavic name, Ziva, means alive and belonged to a goddess of life.
namesakes: Ziva David (Mossad officer turned agent on NCIS)

assoc.t: Ziva David, Mossad officer on NCIS

e.etymology: The Greek short form of Ekaterini and a Russian and Bulgarian form of Ekaterina, the name English knows as Catherine. Its Greek source, Aikaterine, was linked early on with katharos, pure.
From Hebrew Elon, oak tree. In the Old Testament Elon is one of the judges of Israel.
namesakes: Elon Musk (Tesla and SpaceX chief executive)

assoc.t: Elon Musk, Tesla and SpaceX chief
Elon University in North Carolina

e.note: Nearly everyone will connect the name to Elon Musk, a polarizing public figure.

e.etymology: An English occupational surname for someone who brewed ale, now used as a first name alongside Sawyer, Thatcher and Baker.

assoc.t: brewer, the everyday word for a beer maker
Milwaukee Brewers baseball team

e.note: Reads as the ordinary word for someone who makes beer.

e.meaning: pet form of Eleanor, Ellen or Helen
e.etymology: A pet form of Nell, the medieval short form of Eleanor, Ellen and Helen; the N came from the phrase mine Ellen. This spelling is also common in Spanish- and French-speaking countries.
namesakes: Nelly Furtado (singer of I'm Like a Bird)
Nelly Korda (top-ranked golfer and Olympic champion)

assoc.t: Nelly, the St. Louis rapper of Hot in Herre
whoa, Nelly and nervous Nellie, stock phrases

e.note: The rapper Nelly owns the name for many Americans; whoa, Nelly and nervous Nellie jokes are likely.
